title: Son of Adam (Luke 3:15–38)
hookLine: after the baptism, Luke traces Jesus back past Abraham, to Adam, son of God
carry: son of adam, son of god

cards: Luke's family tree runs the wrong way. A family tree usually starts with the oldest name and works down. Luke starts with Jesus, about thirty years old, and climbs.
Son of Joseph, as was supposed. Son of Heli. Son of Matthat.
Back through King David, back through Abraham, back past the flood to Noah, and still he keeps going. A long ladder of fathers, easy to skip.
But read to the very last rung, because of where Luke puts this list, and the strange, beautiful word he ends on.

teach.h: JOHN: ONE MIGHTIER THAN I COMETH.
teach.b: People wonder if John might be the Christ, and he says no: "I indeed baptize you with water; but one mightier than I cometh, the latchet of whose shoes I am not worthy to unloose."
Then Jesus is baptized, and Luke adds that he was praying.

"The heaven was opened, And the Holy Ghost descended in a bodily shape like a dove upon him, and a voice came from heaven, which said, Thou art my beloved Son; in thee I am well pleased." The voice has just said: my Son.
And right there, Luke drops in the genealogy.

teach.h: THE LIST CLIMBS BACK PAST ABRAHAM.
teach.b: Matthew's begins with Abraham and runs forward, a story of Israel's kings. Luke's runs backward and doesn't stop at Abraham.
It ends: "Which was the son of Enos, which was the son of Seth, which was the son of Adam, which was the son of God."
In Genesis, Adam is also the name God gives humankind, male and female together. So some readers hear Luke tying Jesus to every person who has ever lived, the whole human family.

teach.h: WHICH WAS THE SON OF ADAM, WHICH WAS THE SON OF GOD.
teach.b: And Adam is called a son of God too. The voice at the river says this one is my beloved Son; the list underneath says he belongs to everyone.

Between David and Joseph the two lists don't match name for name, and Christians explain that differently: some say Luke follows Mary's family, others point to adoption or old family custom. The texts don't say.
What Luke makes plain is the shape: from the river all the way back to the garden.

how: Some churches read Luke's account of the baptism on the feast of the Baptism of the Lord, and some Christians point to Luke's genealogy as a sign that Jesus belongs to the whole human family.

games.q: you're Luke. the voice from heaven has just said "my beloved Son." what do you write next?
o: a family tree that runs all the way back to Adam.
games.why: Luke places the genealogy right there, climbing from Jesus back to Adam, "the son of God."

practice: Start with your parents, or whoever raised you, then their parents, then one more step back, to names you've heard once, a village, an old photograph, or nothing at all.
Picture them anyway, eight people, sixteen, who worked and worried and prayed or didn't, and keep going back past what anyone remembers, to the human family Luke traces.
If you pray, give thanks for the ones whose names are lost; if not, simply notice how long the line is.

wordCard.voice: Adam, the name Genesis gives both the first man and all humankind, near the top of Luke's family tree.

orig.note: Hebrew: Adam. in Genesis, the first man's name, and in Genesis 5:2 the name given to humankind.
